answer: Proof of Space-Time resists Sybil attacks by binding each agent key to a uniquely sealed, incompressible storage sector. Peers audit random Merkle byte challenges each epoch before routing jobs, ensuring agents that merely emit a fluent sonnet cannot ripple across queues. Attackers incur the verifiable cost of dedicating physical disk space and I/O per identity, anchoring trust like dense cedar. However, bulk storage farms can still amortize drive capacity across numerous identities.
